verdict: Caution: lend selectively to branded, cash-generating hotels and restaurants with LPG-cost pass-through; avoid thin-margin budget eateries and subsidy-dependent operators.
title: Thiruvananthapuram Tourism, Hotels & Restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A hotel or restaurant in Thiruvananthapuram buys gas, food, power and staff, and sells rooms and plates at a price the local market will bear. **Cash arrives daily at the counter; the cost base is largely fixed and energy-heavy.** Commercial LPG is a direct kitchen input, and a fresh hike of Rs 12.50 per cylinder has landed on the industry [1]. So when a proposal lands, check the kitchen's monthly cylinder count and its menu-price revision history; if the operator cannot show a pass-through in the last two quarters, ask how the margin gap is funded.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in location, brand and repeat corporate/MICE demand, not in the building.** Peer results show the money is in pricing power: Leela's Q2 growth was 30% RevPAR growth, entirely ARR-led, on domestic travel and strong MICE demand [6]; ITC Hotels posted consolidated revenue of Rs 1,054 crore, up 26 percent, with EBITDA at Rs 337 crore, up 37 percent [4]. Ventive ran 71 percent occupancy in its international hospitality business [5]. These are peers, not Thiruvananthapuram numbers, so treat them as a benchmark for what a well-run asset can earn, not as local proof.

## What has broken now
**The local signal is cost shock plus thin-margin failure.** Commercial LPG rose again [1], and in March 2026 about 200 hotels in Thiruvananthapuram were reported on the verge of shutdown amid an LPG shortage [3]. In September 2026 the city's first Kudumbashree budget hotel, Ananthapuri Cafe, ceased operations due to mounting debts, with delayed government payouts and a KSEB power disconnection cited [2]. That is a subsidy-and-cashflow failure, not a demand failure. So when a budget-eatery proposal lands, check dependence on government or subsidy receivables; if receivables exceed a month of operating cost, ask for the sanction letter and payment date.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue branded mid-market hotels with corporate and MICE mix, and restaurants with proven menu pricing power.** Avoid subsidy-linked community kitchens and single-outlet budget eateries with no gas-cost pass-through [2][3]. Structure term debt against the property with a clear DSCR, and take monthly stock-and-cash statements, cylinder purchase bills, GST returns and bank statements. **The monthly cylinder bill is your best early read on kitchen economics** [1]. Collect from customer the local ADR, occupancy and F&B margin; the sources give no Thiruvananthapuram-specific figures.

## Early-warning signs
- **Gas bill rising without menu revision** [1]: if two consecutive months show this, reprice the limit or ask for promoter infusion.
- **Power or utility disconnection notices** [2]: any notice means stop fresh disbursement and inspect cash.
- **Subsidy or government receivable ageing** [2]: beyond 30 days, ask for the sanction and expected date.
- **Occupancy or covers slipping while staff cost holds**: ask for the daily sales register.
watch: Bill up with no menu revision -> reprice limit or seek promoter infusion
Disconnection notice -> halt disbursement, inspect cash
Beyond 30 days -> demand sanction letter and payment date
Covers falling with flat staff cost -> review limit
